title: Write a desugarer
hints: Start with `match e:` and one case per class. Anything that is not matched, such as `Lit` and `Var`, is returned unchanged.
A core node rebuilds itself from desugared operands: `case Add(a, b): return Add(desugar(a), desugar(b))`. Do the same for `Mul`, `Exp2` and `Log2`.

The sugar cases: `Sub(a, b)` returns `Add(desugar(a), Mul(desugar(b), Lit(-1.0)))`, `Exp(a)` returns `Exp2(Mul(desugar(a), Lit(1.442695)))` and `Log(a)` returns `Mul(Log2(desugar(a)), Lit(0.6931472))`.
prompt: Same job, new ops, and this time the function is empty. Write desugar so that Sub, Exp and Log become core ops everywhere in the tree: sub a b is add a (mul b -1), exp x is exp2 (mul x 1.442695) and log x is mul (log2 x) 0.6931472.

answer.explain: Every branch rebuilds its node from desugared operands, so the rewrite reaches the whole tree. The three sugar branches build their expansions: `sub a b` becomes `add a (mul b -1)`, `exp x` becomes `exp2 (mul x 1.442695)` and `log x` becomes `mul (log2 x) 0.6931472`. The result contains no sugar at all, so a later pass needs no cases for it.
